question: A cement silo's pressure peaks only when a tanker purges its line at the end of filling, while the vent filter's steady differential pressure is normal. What evidence should an agent collect before attributing the event to the filter?
scenario: A cement silo's pressure peaks only when a tanker purges its line at the end of filling, while the vent filter's steady differential pressure is normal. What evidence should an agent collect before attributing the event to the filter
evidence_required: silo pressure and vent-filter DP trends at second-level timestamps
tanker unloading and purge air pressure/flow log
high-level and inlet shutoff event history
filter element and clean-air outlet inspection
answer_and_decision_guide: Compare time-synchronized silo pressure, tanker purge-air pressure/flow, vent-filter DP, level, shutoff-valve state and pulse-cleaning sequence. Check whether the peak coincides with air-only purge and whether the pressure instrument response is valid. Suspend transfer after an abnormal event and require site/OEM review of the permitted purge sequence rather than increasing relief pressure.
